content:
According to Bloomberg, Apple has increased the monthly and annual fees for AppleCare+ for new Mac and iPad users. Details are as follows.

AppleCare+ price hike affects new iPads and Macs

AppleCare+ is Apple's extended warranty and device protection service, offering additional hardware warranty, technical support, and accidental damage repair.

Bloomberg found that Apple today raised the price of AppleCare+ for Mac and iPad by US$0.50 per month and US$5 per year.

In fact, the new prices are as follows:

New Mac

  • Mac mini: US$4.99 per month or US$49.99 per year
  • Mac Studio: US$7.49 per month or US$74.99 per year
  • iMac: US$7.49 per month or US$74.99 per year
  • MacBook Air: US$6.49 per month or US$64.99 per year
  • 13-inch MacBook Air: US$8.49 per month or US$84.99 per year
  • 15-inch MacBook Air: US$9.49 per month or US$94.99 per year
  • 14-inch MacBook Pro: US$11.49 per month or US$114.99 per year
  • 16-inch MacBook Pro: US$16.49 per month or US$164.99 per year
  • Mac Pro: US$18.99 per month or US$189.99 per year

New iPad

  • iPad and iPad mini: US$6.49 per month or US$64.99 per year
  • 11-inch iPad Air (M3): US$7.49 per month or US$74.99 per year
  • 13-inch iPad Air (M3): US$8.49 per month or US$84.99 per year
  • 11-inch iPad Pro (M5): US$11.49 per month or US$114.99 per year
  • 13-inch iPad Pro (M5): US$12.49 per month or US$124.99 per year

It is worth noting that the new prices only affect new Mac and iPad subscribers. Existing customers will temporarily continue to pay at the old prices.

Apple's multi-device protection plan "AppleCare One" launched last year does not appear to be affected by this adjustment.
